speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury—being caught in a jersey and pulled forcefully—sounds like a classic "jersey finger" where the flexor tendon avulses from the distal phalanx. Since your inflammatory markers are normal, this supports a traumatic etiology over an infection. Can you tell me if you are currently able to flex the tip of that finger on its own, or if it feels like it is slipping out of your grasp? REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray_Right_Hand.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of an avulsion injury combined with the specific inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint while the finger remains extended strongly suggests a "Jersey Finger." The normal inflammatory markers rule out a deep space infection like felon or flexor tenosynovitis. Has your finger been able to touch the tip of the other fingers on your hand since the injury occurred?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor

The history of forceful traction during football combined with your specific inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint is highly characteristic of an avulsion injury. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion of Flexor Digitorum Profundus)
